newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Skala rallies on news of Centrum plans.
newsitem.headline: Skala rallies on news of Centrum plans.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian holding company Skala-Coop Rt jumped to a record level in early trading on Thursday after it announced plans to increase its stake in retail chain Centrum Aruhazak Rt from 25 to 41 percent.

Skala shares opened at 2,550 forints, above yesterday's last price of 2,440 and rose to 2,700, up more than 10 percent. This rise triggered a temporary trading dealingssuspension for ten minutes after which dealings resumed, traders said.
At 1056 GMT Skala shares traded at 2,510 forints, up 70.
Skala said on Wednesday it has offered to subscribe to a one billion forint share package to be issued by retail chain Centrum Aruhazak Rt.
The share issue would bring Centrum's share capital to six billion, while it would allow an additional 16 percent stake to Skala in Centrum.
The one-billion-forint capital increase would be fully subscribed by Skala, which is majority owned by Germany's Tengelmann AG.
